quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Akoustis's opening brief to exclude certain damages opinions of Melissa A. Bennis, redacted (D.I. 476)

quotes.quote: The trial for Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc., DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM commenced on May 6, 2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Minute Entry for Day 7 of a Jury Trial held before Judge Jon P McCalla - Jury Trial held on 5/14/2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Because Plaintiff’s only basis for proving damages to a reasonable certainty is inconsistent with the damages cognizable under the UDTPA, the Defendants’ 50(a) Motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On April 30, 2024, the court denied each party’s Motion to Exclude the Expert Witness Testimony of the other party’s damages expert.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 2, 2024, the court granted Qorvo’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to the validity of the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The complaint alleges Qorvo’s willful infringement of the Cornell patent and seeks remedies including enhanced damages and attorneys’ fees.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 1, 2024, the Company filed a motion for leave to amend its complaint to add Cornell University as a co-plaintiff, as well as a motion to compel financial discovery.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: We are still early in case procedures.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In particular, the theories used by each party's experts result in very disparate estimates of the damages alleged by Corvo. We believe the theories used by our experts are better grounded in the facts and the law. However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: Akoustis’ conduct has not caused Qorvo any legally cognizable damage under the DTSA or North Carolina law
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: The plaintiff seeks an injunction enjoining the Company from the alleged infringement and damages, including punitive and statutory enhanced damages, in an unspecified amount.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The Company can provide no assurance as to the outcome of such trial, and the result may include judgments against the Company for an injunction, significant damages or other relief, such as future royalty payments to Qorvo or restrictions on certain of the Company’s activities.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Minute Entry for Day 7 of a Jury Trial held before Judge Jon P McCalla - Jury Trial held on 5/14/2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Because Plaintiff’s only basis for proving damages to a reasonable certainty is inconsistent with the damages cognizable under the UDTPA, the Defendants’ 50(a) Motion is GRANTED IN PART AND DENIED IN PART. The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA, but has sufficient basis to find injury.
quotes.source: Qorvo v. Akoustis (D. Del. 1:21-cv-01417), Order on the Rule 50(a) motions on unfair-trade-practices damages (D.I. 590)

quotes.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On April 30, 2024, the court denied each party’s Motion to Exclude the Expert Witness Testimony of the other party’s damages expert.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 2, 2024, the court granted Qorvo’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to the validity of the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The complaint alleges Qorvo’s willful infringement of the Cornell patent and seeks remedies including enhanced damages and attorneys’ fees.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 1, 2024, the Company filed a motion for leave to amend its complaint to add Cornell University as a co-plaintiff, as well as a motion to compel financial discovery.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: We are still early in case procedures.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In particular, the theories used by each party's experts result in very disparate estimates of the damages alleged by Corvo. We believe the theories used by our experts are better grounded in the facts and the law. However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.

quotes.quote: Akoustis’ conduct has not caused Qorvo any legally cognizable damage under the DTSA or North Carolina law

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."

nodes.question: Does the court's ruling on the post-trial motions leave the money judgment standing, or set it aside (judgment as a matter of law on liability, or a new trial)?
nodes.label: Does the court's ruling on the post-trial motions leave the money judgment standing, or set it aside (judgment as a matter of law on liability, or a new trial)?
nodes.sub: Without principal measure

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(b); JMOL only where the record lacks the minimum evidence to support the verdict (Lightning Lube v. Witco, 4 F.3d 1153, 1166 (3d Cir. 1993)).

Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(a)(1)(A): after a jury trial the court may grant a new trial on all or some of the issues "for any reason for which a new trial has heretofore been granted in an action at law in federal court." A new trial may be granted even where the evidence is legally sufficient to support the verdict, when the verdict is contrary to the great weight of the evidence, so that a new trial is necessary to prevent a miscarriage of justice (Roebuck v. Drexel Univ., 852 F.2d 715, 735-36 (3d Cir. 1988)). "[N]ew trials because the verdict is against the weight of the evidence are proper only when the record shows that the jury's verdict resulted in a miscarriage of justice or where the verdict, on the record, cries out to be overturned or shocks our conscience" (Williamson v. Consolidated Rail Corp., 926 F.2d 1344, 1353 (3d Cir. 1991)). An award "so grossly excessive as to shock the judicial conscience" is set aside: the court remits it to the maximum recovery that does not shock the judicial conscience, or orders a new trial (Gumbs v. Pueblo Int'l, Inc., 823 F.2d 768, 771-74 (3d Cir. 1987)).

Remittitur is to the maximum the evidence supports, and the plaintiff may refuse it and take a new trial (Hetzel v. Prince William County, 523 U.S. 208 (1998); Kazan v. Wolinski, 721 F.2d 911 (3d Cir. 1983)).

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

nodes.question: Do three or more noteholders file an involuntary bankruptcy petition against the issuer?
nodes.context: after acceleration on the delisting (suspended without a hearing); before the ruling
nodes.label: Holders file after no-action period
nodes.sub: Before ruling · delisting · suspended, no hearing

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

nodes.sub: After ruling · without principal measure · on appeal

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

nodes.question: Does the court's ruling on the post-trial motions leave the money judgment standing, or set it aside (judgment as a matter of law on liability, or a new trial)?
nodes.label: Does the court's ruling on the post-trial motions leave the money judgment standing, or set it aside (judgment as a matter of law on liability, or a new trial)?
nodes.sub: Claimant theory

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(b); JMOL only where the record lacks the minimum evidence to support the verdict (Lightning Lube v. Witco, 4 F.3d 1153, 1166 (3d Cir. 1993)).

Fed. R. Civ. P. 59(a)(1)(A): after a jury trial the court may grant a new trial on all or some of the issues "for any reason for which a new trial has heretofore been granted in an action at law in federal court." A new trial may be granted even where the evidence is legally sufficient to support the verdict, when the verdict is contrary to the great weight of the evidence, so that a new trial is necessary to prevent a miscarriage of justice (Roebuck v. Drexel Univ., 852 F.2d 715, 735-36 (3d Cir. 1988)). "[N]ew trials because the verdict is against the weight of the evidence are proper only when the record shows that the jury's verdict resulted in a miscarriage of justice or where the verdict, on the record, cries out to be overturned or shocks our conscience" (Williamson v. Consolidated Rail Corp., 926 F.2d 1344, 1353 (3d Cir. 1991)). An award "so grossly excessive as to shock the judicial conscience" is set aside: the court remits it to the maximum recovery that does not shock the judicial conscience, or orders a new trial (Gumbs v. Pueblo Int'l, Inc., 823 F.2d 768, 771-74 (3d Cir. 1987)).

Remittitur is to the maximum the evidence supports, and the plaintiff may refuse it and take a new trial (Hetzel v. Prince William County, 523 U.S. 208 (1998); Kazan v. Wolinski, 721 F.2d 911 (3d Cir. 1983)).

nodes.question: When the stock is delisted, do the holders declare the notes due, require repurchase, or neither?
nodes.context: suspended without a hearing; stayed
nodes.label: Holders act on delisting
nodes.sub: Suspended, no hearing · stayed

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(b)): the common stock is not listed on an Eligible Market; it takes effect without notice or grace period.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

Fundamental Change repurchase (§10.01): delisting lets each holder require repurchase at 100% of principal plus accrued interest in cash; notice within 20 business days, repurchase 20-35 business days after notice; failure to repurchase is an Event of Default.

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.

nodes.question: Does the judgment debtor move for a stay on a bond or other security?
nodes.context: after the ruling; on appeal
nodes.label: Akoustis moves for stay
nodes.sub: After ruling · claimant theory · on appeal

steps.text: Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(b): a party may obtain a stay by providing a bond or other security; "The stay takes effect when the court approves the bond or other security".

A supersedeas bond secures "the whole amount of the judgment remaining unsatisfied, costs on the appeal, interest, and damages for delay" (Southern Track & Pump, Inc. v. Terex Corp., C.A. No. 08-543-LPS (D. Del.), quoting Poplar Grove Planting & Ref. Co. v. Bache Halsey Stuart, 600 F.2d 1189, 1191 (5th Cir. 1979)). The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

The court may accept reduced or alternative security for good cause (Dillon v. City of Chicago, 866 F.2d 902, 904-05 (7th Cir. 1988); Poplar Grove).

quotes.quote: An adverse result in the matters described above would have a material adverse effect on the Company and its business and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Even if ultimately settled or resolved in the Company’s favor, the matters described above and other possible future actions have resulted in significant expenses
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Any out-of-court settlement of the above matters or other actions may also have an adverse effect on the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations, including, but not limited to, substantial expenses, the payment of royalties, licensing or other fees payable to third parties, or restrictions on its ability to develop, manufacture, and sell its products.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In November 2023, the Company announced that it had undertaken significant expense reductions and cost-saving measures to reduce its operating cash flow burn.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Additionally, the Company estimates that approximately $ 0.7 million of additional cash is needed to complete construction in progress assets that are currently not in service, which construction has been paused as part of these cost-savings initiatives.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In January 2024, the Company completed a public offering of its common stock raising $ 10.4 million in net proceeds. Additionally, the Company is re-activating its at-the-market equity offering program
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: the Company will need to raise significant additional capital to sustain its business
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On June 9, 2022, Akoustis Technologies, Inc. (the “Company”) issued $44.0 million aggregate principal amount of its 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 (the “Notes”) guaranteed by its wholly-owned subsidiary, Akoustis, Inc.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: The Notes bear interest at a rate of 6.0% per year until maturity on June 15, 2027 (the “Maturity Date”).
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: is payable semi-annually in arrears on June 15 and December 15 of each year, beginning on December 15, 2022. At the Company’s option, interest may be paid in cash and/or freely tradable shares of the Company’s common stock, subject to certain limitations
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: The Company will settle conversions of the Notes through delivery of shares of common stock of the Company in accordance with the terms of the Indenture. The initial conversion rate for the Notes is 212.3142 shares of common stock (subject to adjustment as provided in the Indenture) per $1,000 principal amount of the Notes, which is equal to an initial conversion price of approximately $4.71 per share.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: If any Notes are converted prior to June 9, 2025 (the “Interest Make-Whole Date”), the Company will make a payment to the holder of such Notes equal to the sum of the remaining scheduled payments of interest that would have been made on the Notes to be converted had such Notes remained outstanding from the conversion date through and including the Interest Make-Whole Date. The Company will have the option to pay such Interest Make-Whole Payment in cash and/or common stock
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: The Company may redeem the Notes, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time on or after June 9, 2023 at a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest on such principal
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: the closing sale price per share of the Company’s common stock is greater than 150% of the then-effective conversion price
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: will not exceed 19.99% of the Company’s common stock outstanding on the trading day immediately preceding the date of the purchase agreement entered into with respect to the sale of the Securities, unless the Company obtains the requisite stockholder approval pursuant to the rules of the Nasdaq Capital Market.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: If the Company redeems the Notes prior to the Interest Make-Whole Date, the holder will also receive an interest make-whole payment
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: CapEx spending for Q3 was $0.3 million, and cash use and operating activities was $7.8 million, representing a 31% reduction over the December quarter as a result of our expense reduction effort. We are guiding the June quarter revenue to be flat to down 5%
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: all of which we estimate will reduce our operating cash flow burn rate by an additional 30% sequentially in the June quarter. Given the top-line projections, the current timing of the CHIP's ITC refunds, and the full impact of recent cost savings, we expect to be operating cash flow breakeven within the next nine months.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: The trial for Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc., DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM commenced on May 6, 2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Minute Entry for Day 7 of a Jury Trial held before Judge Jon P McCalla - Jury Trial held on 5/14/2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In particular, the theories used by each party's experts result in very disparate estimates of the damages alleged by Corvo. We believe the theories used by our experts are better grounded in the facts and the law. However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: Akoustis’ conduct has not caused Qorvo any legally cognizable damage under the DTSA or North Carolina law
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On April 30, 2024, the court denied each party’s Motion to Exclude the Expert Witness Testimony of the other party’s damages expert.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 2, 2024, the court granted Qorvo’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to the validity of the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The plaintiff seeks an injunction enjoining the Company from the alleged infringement and damages, including punitive and statutory enhanced damages, in an unspecified amount.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The Company can provide no assurance as to the outcome of such trial, and the result may include judgments against the Company for an injunction, significant damages or other relief, such as future royalty payments to Qorvo or restrictions on certain of the Company’s activities.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In November 2023, the Company announced that it had undertaken significant expense reductions and cost-saving measures to reduce its operating cash flow burn.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Additionally, the Company estimates that approximately $ 0.7 million of additional cash is needed to complete construction in progress assets that are currently not in service, which construction has been paused as part of these cost-savings initiatives.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In January 2024, the Company completed a public offering of its common stock raising $ 10.4 million in net proceeds. Additionally, the Company is re-activating its at-the-market equity offering program
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: the Company will need to raise significant additional capital to sustain its business
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

steps.text: Indenture §7.06 (Limitation on Suits): "No Holder shall have any right to institute any proceeding, judicial or otherwise, in respect of this Indenture, or for the appointment of a receiver or trustee, or for any other remedy hereunder (other than in the case of an Event of Default specified in clause (j) or (k) of Section 7.01), unless: (a) the Holder of a Note gives to the Trustee written notice of a continuing Event of Default; (b) the Holders of at least 25% in Principal Amount of the then outstanding Notes make a written request to the Trustee to pursue the remedy; (c) such Holder of a Note or Holders of Notes offer and, if requested, provide to the Trustee indemnity reasonably satisfactory to the Trustee against any loss, liability or expense; (d) the Trustee does not comply with the request within 60 days after receipt of the request and the offer and, if requested, the provision of indemnity; and (e) during such 60-day period the Majority Holders do not give the Trustee a direction inconsistent with the request."

Indenture §7.07 (Unconditional Rights of Holders of Notes to Receive Payment): "Notwithstanding any other provision of this Indenture, the right of any Holder to receive payment of the Principal, the Redemption Price, or Interest, in respect of the Notes held by such Holder, on or after the respective due dates expressed in the Notes or any Redemption Date, as applicable, and to convert the Notes in accordance with ARTICLE 9, or to bring suit for the enforcement of any such payment on or after such respective dates or the right to convert, shall not be impaired or affected adversely without the consent of such Holder."
11 U.S.C. §303(b)(1): where the debtor has 12 or more creditors, an involuntary petition is filed by three or more creditors holding noncontingent, undisputed claims above the statutory threshold.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In November 2023, the Company announced that it had undertaken significant expense reductions and cost-saving measures to reduce its operating cash flow burn.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In November 2023, the Company announced that it had undertaken significant expense reductions and cost-saving measures to reduce its operating cash flow burn.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Additionally, the Company estimates that approximately $ 0.7 million of additional cash is needed to complete construction in progress assets that are currently not in service, which construction has been paused as part of these cost-savings initiatives.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In January 2024, the Company completed a public offering of its common stock raising $ 10.4 million in net proceeds. Additionally, the Company is re-activating its at-the-market equity offering program
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.

quotes.quote: the Company will need to raise significant additional capital to sustain its business

steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(i)): final money judgments above the threshold, excluding amounts covered by insurance, remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for the stated period, during which execution is not effectively stayed; it takes effect on notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of principal.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

quotes.quote: An adverse result in the matters described above would have a material adverse effect on the Company and its business and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code.

quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. quotes.quote: On June 9, 2022, Akoustis Technologies, Inc. (the “Company”) issued $44.0 million aggregate principal amount of its 6.0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 (the “Notes”) guaranteed by its wholly-owned subsidiary, Akoustis, Inc.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: The Notes bear interest at a rate of 6.0% per year until maturity on June 15, 2027 (the “Maturity Date”).
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: is payable semi-annually in arrears on June 15 and December 15 of each year, beginning on December 15, 2022. At the Company’s option, interest may be paid in cash and/or freely tradable shares of the Company’s common stock, subject to certain limitations
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: The Company will settle conversions of the Notes through delivery of shares of common stock of the Company in accordance with the terms of the Indenture. The initial conversion rate for the Notes is 212.3142 shares of common stock (subject to adjustment as provided in the Indenture) per $1,000 principal amount of the Notes, which is equal to an initial conversion price of approximately $4.71 per share.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: If any Notes are converted prior to June 9, 2025 (the “Interest Make-Whole Date”), the Company will make a payment to the holder of such Notes equal to the sum of the remaining scheduled payments of interest that would have been made on the Notes to be converted had such Notes remained outstanding from the conversion date through and including the Interest Make-Whole Date. The Company will have the option to pay such Interest Make-Whole Payment in cash and/or common stock
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: The Company may redeem the Notes, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time on or after June 9, 2023 at a redemption price equal to 100% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest on such principal
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: the closing sale price per share of the Company’s common stock is greater than 150% of the then-effective conversion price
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: will not exceed 19.99% of the Company’s common stock outstanding on the trading day immediately preceding the date of the purchase agreement entered into with respect to the sale of the Securities, unless the Company obtains the requisite stockholder approval pursuant to the rules of the Nasdaq Capital Market.

quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 8-K, June 2022 (6.0% convertible senior notes due 2027)

quotes.quote: Minute Entry for Day 7 of a Jury Trial held before Judge Jon P McCalla - Jury Trial held on 5/14/2024.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In particular, the theories used by each party's experts result in very disparate estimates of the damages alleged by Corvo. We believe the theories used by our experts are better grounded in the facts and the law. However, if the jury adopts the theories of Corvo's experts, it is possible the jury will issue an eight-figure verdict. For that reason, this litigation may have a significant impact on the company. including its value, operations, and ability to raise money.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: The trial is expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: Akoustis’ conduct has not caused Qorvo any legally cognizable damage under the DTSA or North Carolina law
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies fiscal third quarter 2024 earnings call, 13 May 2024 (machine transcript)

quotes.quote: On April 25, 2024, the court granted the Company’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to Qorvo’s false patent marking and RICO claims, but denied the remainder of the Company’s motion.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On April 30, 2024, the court denied each party’s Motion to Exclude the Expert Witness Testimony of the other party’s damages expert.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: On May 2, 2024, the court granted Qorvo’s Motion for Partial Summary Judgment with respect to the validity of the ‘018 Patent and the ‘755 Patent.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The plaintiff seeks an injunction enjoining the Company from the alleged infringement and damages, including punitive and statutory enhanced damages, in an unspecified amount.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: The Company can provide no assurance as to the outcome of such trial, and the result may include judgments against the Company for an injunction, significant damages or other relief, such as future royalty payments to Qorvo or restrictions on certain of the Company’s activities.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In November 2023, the Company announced that it had undertaken significant expense reductions and cost-saving measures to reduce its operating cash flow burn.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Additionally, the Company estimates that approximately $ 0.7 million of additional cash is needed to complete construction in progress assets that are currently not in service, which construction has been paused as part of these cost-savings initiatives.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In January 2024, the Company completed a public offering of its common stock raising $ 10.4 million in net proceeds. Additionally, the Company is re-activating its at-the-market equity offering program
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. steps.text: Event of Default (§7.01(i)): final money judgments above the threshold, excluding amounts covered by insurance, remain undischarged, unpaid or unstayed for the stated period, during which execution is not effectively stayed; it takes effect on notice by the trustee or holders of 25% of principal.

Acceleration (§7.02): on an Event of Default the trustee or holders of 25% may declare the notes due; a bankruptcy petition makes them due automatically; holders of a majority may rescind once every default is cured, and a judgment default is cured by payment, discharge or a stay.

quotes.quote: As of March 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $ 15.2 million and working capital of $ 10.3 million. In the absence of additional liquidity, the Company anticipates that its existing cash resources, with a continued focus on cash conservation, is sufficient to fund its operations into the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Furthermore, an adverse judgment against the Company in the trial with respect to Qorvo Inc. vs. Akoustis Technologies, Inc. DE Case 1:21-cv-01417-JPM , as described below under Note 14. Commitments and Contingencies (the “Delaware Trial”), would reduce the amount of time that the Company could continue operating with its current cash resources, and create an urgent need for additional liquidity or result in the Company’s curtailing or ceasing operations and seeking protection by filing a voluntary petition for relief under the Bankruptcy Code. These matters raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year from the date of this filing.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: (v) interest and principal payments related to its $ 44.0 million aggregate principal amount of outstanding convertible notes and $ 4.0 million promissory note.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: To the extent that the outcome of the trial includes judgments against the Company for significant damages or other relief, the Company’s liquidity will be additionally and severely constrained.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In November 2023, the Company announced that it had undertaken significant expense reductions and cost-saving measures to reduce its operating cash flow burn.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Additionally, the Company estimates that approximately $ 0.7 million of additional cash is needed to complete construction in progress assets that are currently not in service, which construction has been paused as part of these cost-savings initiatives.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: In January 2024, the Company completed a public offering of its common stock raising $ 10.4 million in net proceeds. Additionally, the Company is re-activating its at-the-market equity offering program
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: Except for the $ 48.0 million of common stock remaining available to be sold under its ATM Sales Agreement with Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, and Roth Capital Partners, LLC, the Company has no commitments or arrangements to obtain any additional funds, and there can be no assurance such funds will be available on acceptable terms or at all.
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024

quotes.quote: the Company will need to raise significant additional capital to sustain its business
quotes.source: Akoustis Technologies Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024
